purpose: Verify that a standard CloudEvents envelope can feed the existing cross-application bridge without losing identity, provenance or safety controls.

activities.label: map the standardized envelope into the existing cross-application contract
attack adapter input identity provenance permissions and external execution
record equivalence and the no-live-api boundary

queries.expression: does the adapter preserve the envelope event identity and canonical order
does the mapped payload satisfy the existing GitLab to Mattermost bridge contract
does the adapter retain dry-run, permission, provenance and independent verification gates

assumptions: The 068 local envelope is the only input event stream for this fixture.
The 065 compiler is reused as an existing contract and is not copied into the adapter.
The destination remains Mattermost dry-run and no external API is contacted.
The source snapshot is synthetic and contains no human data.
Preserving event identity and source references is more important than hiding mapping steps.
kill_tests: Missing required input event blocks the adapter.
External destination execution blocks the adapter.
Missing claim provenance blocks the bridge.
Stale precondition blocks the proposed action.
Missing destination permission blocks the bridge.
Detached required event identity blocks the adapter.
An undeclared input envelope blocks the adapter.
unknowns: Whether GitLab and Mattermost production APIs can emit and consume this exact mapping.
Whether a real adapter needs signatures, schema registry or transactional delivery.
Which institutional pair should be the first non-synthetic adapter.
Whether the same mapping can be reused for OpenEMR and Nextcloud without domain-specific fields.
